title: Longest-example memory for automatic learning
formal: If an automatic language family is identifiable in the limit from positive data by an automatic learner with unrestricted memory, is it also learnable with memory length at most the longest example seen plus a constant?

import_provenance.original_title: Does extra automatic memory beyond the longest example help learning?
import_provenance.original_statement: If an automatic family of languages is identifiable in the limit from positive examples by an automatic learner with unrestricted memory, must it also be learnable when its memory length is bounded by the longest example seen, up to an additive constant? The learner must succeed on every text enumerating the target language; equivalent automatic hypothesis codings may be chosen.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: This is the positive-data-only model. With arbitrary negative counterexamples, longest-example-sized memory is already sufficient for every automatic family.
